notes: This is the synthesis-test region for the very-tight feather variant. halo_presence is a clean 5 — there is no bright luminance halo around the Red Bull wordmark; the canonical Melbourne floor halo case is fully absent. However edge_seam_visibility is the weak axis here (3, regressing from P3-A5's 5): with alpha_feather=2 the patch boundary has a thin but perceptible perimeter line where the Red Bull rectangle meets the surrounding court paint, particularly on the top edge of the patch in mid/late strips. mask_dilate=8 is too aggressive for feather=2 — it trims the substrate match too tight, leaving a hard step. BTN's stable per-frame H prevents this from walking (so it doesn't pop the way line-based P3-A4/a2 did), but a viewer scrubbing slowly will notice the rectangular footprint. Texture match to the matte court paint stays solid; player contact shadow unchanged from prior runs (mark stays opaque under feet). Verdict on the experiment: tight feather successfully eliminates halo, but introduces a low-grade seam — a worse trade than P3-A5 overall.
